scope: 5 reversed protosegments (segmentids 0016558, 0343093-0343096); LION gdb: one proto-segment row on each (nodes, XY, left/right AtomicPolygon)
description: Prod writes a centerline's proto-segments one after another from one feature object, and each reversed proto off the borough boundary reverses that object's shape in place once its values are set (CenterlineExtractFile.cs:3801-3842, SwapFeatureGeometry :4953; LIONExtractorClass.cs:159-176). The next proto starts from the reversed shape, so the second of two reversed protos on a segment comes out unreversed (nodes, XY, sectional maps and left/right fields; its level codes, traffic direction and curve flag follow its own flag). We reproduce prod by default; the fix (dbt var fix_reversed_proto_pairs, default false) orients each proto by its own FROM_TO_INDICATOR, and is off until GR and GSS agree to roll it out. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-12): 5 LION records, the second reversed proto on each of segments 0016558 and 0343093-0343096, on 26c.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_reversed_proto_pairs (off)

scope: 10 non-street proto-segments inside Randall's Island, left and right zip
description: A proto-segment off the borough boundary takes its parent's stored zip (CenterlineExtractFile.cs:3188, 3851-3855), and a shoreline or non-street feature parent never stores one (it looks its zip up when written, NonStreetFeatureExtractFile.cs:118-128), so prod leaves both zips blank, where the spec says the proto copies its parent's zip (10035, the only zip on the island). We reproduce prod by default; the fix (dbt var fix_nonstreet_proto_zip, default false) writes the zip, and is off until GR and GSS agree to roll it out. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-09): 10 LION records, all FEATURE_TYPE 8 proto-segments on face 0064, on 26c.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_nonstreet_proto_zip (off)

scope: Curve flag on single-arc shoreline, subway and rail segments
description: Each of these segments is one circular arc end to end. Prod writes I only when the source shape has more than two points (ShorelineExtractFile.cs:422, GetHasShapePoints), following the spec's "shape points" wording, so a single arc stays blank, though it is curved. We reproduce prod by default; the fix (dbt var fix_single_arc_curve_flag, default false) writes I, and is off until GR and GSS agree to roll it out. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-07): 253 LION records on 26c (shoreline 200, subway 33, rail 20). Which is right is a question for GR.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_single_arc_curve_flag (off)

scope: BOE LGC pointer on segments whose BOE-preferred LGC is above 9
description: Prod returns BOE LGC pointer 1 whenever the segment's BOE-preferred LGC value is above 9 (its code caps the LGC value, not the pointer position; CenterlineExtractFile.cs:1321), where the spec says the position of that LGC. We reproduce prod by default; the fix (dbt var fix_boe_lgc_pointer, default false) writes the position, and is off until GR and GSS agree to roll it out. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-06): 568 LION records, all in Queens, on 26c.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_boe_lgc_pointer (off)

scope: Segment sequence number (SeqNum) on non-street features and on proto-segments whose feature type makes them non-street features (FEATURE_TYPE 3, 4, 7, 8), on faces numbered in the Queens extract
description: Prod numbers these on the fly, one counter per borough and face code carried through the borough extracts of one session. Prod's LION gdb matches numbering all five boroughs in one session, but its LION .dat files match a fresh session for Queens and Staten Island, so prod's two outputs disagree on these records: 1,968 LION gdb records on 26c, every one on a face numbered in the Queens extract. We reproduce prod by default: the LION gdb is numbered in its own extract sessions (dbt var lion_gdb_seqnum_extract_sessions, default one session for all five boroughs) and the LION .dat files in theirs (lion_seqnum_extract_sessions). With the default there is no difference; setting lion_gdb_seqnum_extract_sessions to the .dat files' sessions numbers the gdb like the .dat files, which Geosupport reads. Every build's log reports the sessions and the LION gdb records numbered differently from the .dat files (CSCL-LOG-OURS-22): 1,968 on 26c.
decision: match prod by default (gdb in one session); the .dat files' numbering behind lion_gdb_seqnum_extract_sessions

scope: altnames rows for Join_IDs only one side's LION carries
description: 10 altnames rows on 26c belong to Join_IDs that only one side's LION has, so they follow the LION differences rather than an altnames rule.
decision: match prod

scope: Join_ID padding on the lion layer (221,078 non-SAF rows on 26c)
description: The spec (ETL spec 2.7.3) and prod's ETL make a non-SAF Join_ID 15 characters, ending in two spaces (ExtractorClass.cs:3781, GetBytesJoinID), but prod's distribution tool strips them on the lion layer (BytesLION_CSCL_workflow_tool_PUB.py:127-141, RemoveTrailingSpaces, called at :615); its altnames strip (ImportLION2_ToGDB, :326-336) is commented out (:621), so prod's altnames layer keeps the padding. We reproduce prod by default: the lion layer's non-SAF Join_IDs have no trailing spaces and the altnames layer keeps them. The dbt var pad_lion_join_id (default false) keeps the padding on the lion layer too, as the spec says. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the rows it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-24): 221,078 lion layer rows on 26c. The comparison trims both sides either way, so it reports no diff with the var on either.
decision: match prod by default (lion layer Join_ID unpadded); spec padding behind pad_lion_join_id (off)

scope: Coincident segment count where a subway or rail segment coincides with a centerline: 2 subway and rail records by default (8103717, 0245781), 10 with fix_coincident_seg_count on; gdb SegCount on 2 centerlines that nearly coincide with another centerline (0133914, 0161031)
description: Prod's count on a centerline is the source count less each underground (ROW_TYPE 1) subway or rail segment at the centerline's midpoint that Esri's shape-equality test finds equal to it, with no floor (CenterlineExtractFile.cs:2528-2610), so 4 centerlines come out 0 on 26c (0359093, 0297614, 0327255, 0032941) where the spec's count is an integer above 0. Two shapes each within 0.0003 ft of the other reproduce prod's test on every 26c centerline. We reproduce prod by default; the dbt var fix_coincident_seg_count (default false) subtracts the subway and rail segments within 1 ft of the centerline's midpoint instead, only when the source count is above 1, as ours did. With it off there is no difference on centerlines; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-23): 8 LION records on 26c, the 4 zeros and 4 on Flatbush Avenue and Eastern Parkway (0029283, 0188023, 0149383, 0149678) where a subway made of many short arcs lies within 1 ft of the centerline but up to 0.0008 ft off it. Either way, 2 subway and rail segments that are one circular arc over a centerline of two arcs on the same circle (8103717, 0245781, within 0.00001 ft) count the centerline in ours and not in prod, though prod finds a two-arc centerline equal to a one-arc subway (0251993); no tolerance reproduces that. The gdb SegCount has the same test for two centerlines on the same nodes: ours counts them within 0.0003 ft, and prod counts some pairs up to 0.0004 ft apart but not others, on the densified or the true curves, so no tolerance reproduces it.
decision: match prod by default (shape equality, no floor); ours behind fix_coincident_seg_count (off)

scope: House numbers on generic segments (SegmentTyp G) and their SAF replicants
description: The spec (ETL spec 2.7.3) zeroes all eight house-number fields on generic segments, and so does the legacy tool's rule, but prod's LION gdb keeps the source's house numbers. The legacy tool's zeroing lives in ImportLION2_ToGDB (BytesLION_CSCL_workflow_tool_PUB.py:326; SegmentTyp IN ('G', 'F') OR FeatureTyp NOT IN ('0', '6', 'W') at :353, eight CalculateFields at :354-361), but the tool's main flow never calls it: the call at :621 is commented out. Prod's ETL zeroes a generic segment's house numbers and then overwrites them with the source's (ExtractorClass.cs:2993-3072; the early return was commented out in 2012 so generics would keep their addresses). On 26c every generic record in prod matches the source's values: 5,743 have house numbers and the other 7,849 have none in the source either. We reproduce prod by default; the dbt var zero_generic_house_numbers (default false) zeroes them, as the spec does. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-15): 5,743 LION gdb records on 26c, 342 of them SAF replicants. The LION .dat copies the source's house numbers on generic segments too, in prod and ours. Which is right is a question for GR.
decision: match prod by default (G keeps its house numbers); spec zeroing behind zero_generic_house_numbers (off)

scope: Left/right AtomicPolygon and the fields derived from it, on about 100 segments
description: Prod takes a segment's left/right AtomicPolygons from points 2 ft either side of its midpoint; the probe overshoots into the AtomicPolygon behind where the adjacent one is shallow (corners, slivers), so census, district and locational-status fields follow the wrong AtomicPolygon. The fix (dbt var fix_lion_lr_from_topology, default false) takes them from the AtomicPolygon topology edges the segment runs along instead, and is off until GR and GSS agree to roll it out. We reproduce prod by default: with it off there is no difference. Every build's log reports the records the fix would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-08): 101 LION records (100 segments) on 26c; with it on, 100 LION .dat records and 104 LION gdb rows differ from prod.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_lion_lr_from_topology (off)

scope: Special address flag on Bronx record 236590241972
description: Prod's value on this record doesn't match the source. GR checked it against the source and confirmed ours.
decision: keep ours

scope: Special address flag on ramp protosegment, segment 174704 (Queens)
description: Prod gives a ramp proto-segment (ALT_SEGDATA_TYPE R) the SAF records it attributes to its centerline's proto-segments: AltSegmentData SAF rows with the proto's LIONKEY and address points whose B7SC_ACTUAL starts with the proto's B5SC (CenterlineExtractFile.cs:2716-2737, 2748-2762). The ramp on 174704 shares its centerline's street code with two B address points, so prod prints B; the legacy rule says ramps never carry the flag. We reproduce prod by default; the fix (dbt var fix_ramp_proto_special_address, default false) leaves it blank, and is off until GR and GSS agree to roll it out. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-13): 1 LION record on 26c.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_ramp_proto_special_address (off)

scope: SAF rows of SECURITY_LEVEL 3 CommonPlaces (5 on 26c)
description: Prod's SAF dat drops CommonPlaces with SECURITY_LEVEL 3, but its LION gdb still writes their SAF replicant rows (and counts them in SegCount). Ours copies prod: kept in the LION gdb, dropped from the SAF dat. Whether the gdb should drop them too is a question for GR.
decision: match prod

scope: Centerline protosegments whose street code has a face code only in FeatureName (none on 26c)
description: Prod means to write such a proto-segment with its FeatureName face code and log a warning (CSCL-LOG-LION-15), but compares the table name as stored with a lowercased one (CenterlineExtractFile.cs:3487 vs :3501), looks in StreetName again, finds no face code and drops the proto from the LION .dat and the LION gdb (LIONExtractorClass.cs:443-458, CSCL-LOG-LION-19). We reproduce prod by default (dropped, logged LION-19); the fix (dbt var fix_featurename_face_code_protos, default false) writes it with the FeatureName face code and logs LION-15, and is off until GR and GSS agree to roll it out. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the protos it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-14): none on 26c.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_featurename_face_code_protos (off)

scope: Records with a field value longer than its slot (none on 26c)
description: Prod doesn't write the longer record: it throws on a value longer than its slot (ExtractorClass.cs:1985-1986, CSCL.ETL.Extractor), its catch at :2051 rethrows, and the per-borough feature loop (:1434-1471) doesn't catch it, so the whole extract aborts. Ours cuts the value to its slot, so every record stays 400 characters, logs the record and carries on.
decision: keep ours

scope: House numbers on SegmentTyp F segments and their SAF replicants
description: The legacy tool's rule zeroes all eight house-number fields on SegmentTyp F as well as G, but prod's LION gdb keeps them. The legacy tool's zeroing lives in ImportLION2_ToGDB (BytesLION_CSCL_workflow_tool_PUB.py:326; SegmentTyp IN ('G', 'F') OR FeatureTyp NOT IN ('0', '6', 'W') at :353, eight CalculateFields at :354-361), but the tool's main flow never calls it: the call at :621 is commented out. The spec (ETL spec 2.7.3) zeroes generic segments (SEGMENT_TYPE G) and never names F. On 26c the one F record with house numbers, the SAF A replicant of segment 0346291 (ELIOT AVENUE, Join_ID 44349001000000A, 93-001 to 93-099 / 93-000 to 93-098), keeps them in prod. No F segment has house numbers of its own on 26c. We reproduce prod by default; the dbt var zero_f_segment_house_numbers (default false) applies the legacy rule to F too. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-10): 1 LION gdb record on 26c. The spec's other zeroing rules differ from the legacy tool's too: it zeroes non-physical centerlines (RW_TYPE 12, including paper streets and faux segments), not covered here, and applies the FeatureTyp test (other than null, 6 or W) to proto-segments only, where the legacy tool applies it to every segment (CSCL-LION-29). Which is right, and what SEGMENT_TYPE F is, is a question for GR.
decision: match prod by default (F keeps its house numbers); legacy rule behind zero_f_segment_house_numbers (off)

scope: High house numbers (LHi_Hyphen/RHi_Hyphen, ToLeft/ToRight) on S and V replicants of HYPHEN_TYPE R address points (9 on 26c)
description: Prod's gdb writer takes an R address point's range from a dash in HOUSE_NUMBER (ExtractorClass.cs:5128-5132, SetSAFStreetNameAndCode), the encoding the spec describes, but CSCL stores the range's end in HOUSE_NUMBER_RANGE, so prod writes the low house number and no high one (e.g. segment 0012585's V replicant: 430 and no high house number, where HOUSE_NUMBER_RANGE is 432). We reproduce prod by default; the fix (dbt var fix_hyphen_r_high_house_number, default false) writes HOUSE_NUMBER_RANGE as the high house number. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-18): 9 LION gdb records on 26c.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_hyphen_r_high_house_number (off)

scope: Census tract and block fields (1990-2020) and community district on reversed proto-segments (29 rows on 26c)
description: On a reversed proto-segment prod's gdb swaps the nodes and the left/right AtomicPolygons, as its LION .dat does, but reads the census and community district fields from the AtomicPolygons it found on the shape before the reversal (ExtractorClass.cs:3934 and 2390-2412, SetBytesCensusTract), so they belong to the opposite AtomicPolygon and disagree with prod's own .dat. On the second reversed proto of each CSCL-LION-01 segment the first one had already reversed the shape, so prod's census fields there come out the .dat's way round while its AtomicPolygons don't. We reproduce prod by default; the fix (dbt var fix_reversed_proto_census_fields, default false) writes them with the record's own sides, as the .dat. With it off there is no difference, with fix_reversed_proto_pairs on or off; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-17): 29 LION gdb records on 26c (24 with fix_reversed_proto_pairs on).
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_reversed_proto_census_fields (off)

scope: LSubSect/RSubSect, PhysicalID and GenericID on segments edited 2026-07-24 to 2026-07-27 (12 rows on 26c)
description: Prod's LION gdb has older values than prod's own LION .dat on these segments; ours matches the .dat. Every such source edit falls between 2026-07-24 and 2026-07-27, the end of our extract, so prod's gdb most likely came from an earlier extract than its flat files.
decision: keep ours

scope: L_PD_Service_Area on 5 Manhattan centerlines that lie on a housing-police beat boundary, 9 rows (0003132, 0003134, 0003139 and 0006404 prod '4' where ours is blank; 0003140 prod blank where ours is '4')
description: Prod's LION gdb contradicts prod's own LION .dat here: the .dat (L97/L98) has the housing-police service area on one side only, and ours matches it on both outputs, as the spec says (BL115/BL116 same as L97/L98). Prod writes both from the same beat features in the same pass (CenterlineExtractFile.cs:4550-4670 sets them while writing L97/L98; ExtractorClass.cs:4348-4377 reads them back for the gdb), so the code can't produce the split. Probing them against the 26b NYPD beat layer gives prod's gdb values on all 9 rows: the beat boundaries at the Baruch Houses and Catherine Slip moved between 26b and 26c. Four other beat edits from the same period do show in prod's gdb, so it was most likely built from a beat layer partway through those edits, older than its .dat's: the same family as CSCL-LION-27 (prod's gdb built from an older extract than its flat files). Nowhere else does prod's gdb disagree with its .dat on this field.
decision: keep ours

scope: House numbers on segments of a FeatureTyp other than 0, 6 or W and their SAF replicants
description: The legacy tool's rule zeroes all eight house-number fields where FeatureTyp NOT IN ('0', '6', 'W'), as well as on SegmentTyp G and F, but prod's LION gdb keeps the source's house numbers on every row. The legacy tool's zeroing lives in ImportLION2_ToGDB (BytesLION_CSCL_workflow_tool_PUB.py:326; SegmentTyp IN ('G', 'F') OR FeatureTyp NOT IN ('0', '6', 'W') at :353, eight CalculateFields at :354-361), but the tool's main flow never calls it: the call at :621 is commented out. Prod's ETL zeroes house numbers and then overwrites them with the source's on every branch (ExtractorClass.cs SetBytesNormalizedHouseNumbers, from :2988: generics, RW_TYPE 12 and proto-segments). The spec (ETL spec 2.7.3) applies the FeatureTyp test (other than null, 6 or W) to proto-segments only. On 26c 184 LION gdb records (178 segments) of FeatureTyp 5, 9, A and C have house numbers in the source and keep them in prod: 32, 97, 1 and 54 records; every other record of those FeatureTyps has none in the source either. We reproduce prod by default; the dbt var zero_feature_type_house_numbers (default false) zeroes them, as the legacy rule does, and with zero_generic_house_numbers and zero_f_segment_house_numbers on too the build applies the legacy tool's whole rule. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-25). The LION .dat copies the source's house numbers on these segments, in prod and ours. Whether the published gdb should zero non-street house numbers at all is a question for GR.
decision: match prod by default (non-street FeatureTyp keeps its house numbers); legacy rule behind zero_feature_type_house_numbers (off)

scope: Part count, SHAPE_Length and outline on nynta2020, nycdta2020, nypp and nypuma2020, and a few nycc and nymc districts
description: Prod's polygons carry hairline slivers, about 0.0001 ft wide and under 0.3 sq ft each, along their outlines, as separate parts and as spikes off a ring: 460 parts on nynta2020, 356 on nycdta2020, 207 on nypp and 6 on nypuma2020. They add parts and SHAPE_Length but no area. Ours has none.
decision: keep ours

scope: nybid BIDs 44 and 56; nyhez zones 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and X; nycdwi districts 484 and 502
description: These source polygons are invalid (rings that cross, or a shell inside another shell). Prod copies these layers' source feature classes feature by feature, unclipped (GDBExtractorClass.cs:952-957), so it publishes them as stored; its SHAPE_Area is Esri's area of the stored shape, which counts a shell inside a shell as a hole (BID 56: 4,342,991 sq ft, where the raw rings give 4,361,376). We reproduce prod by default: those features are published as stored, with SHAPE_Area and SHAPE_Length from the valid polygon, which match prod's. The dbt var make_valid_district_polygons (default false) publishes them valid instead (st_makevalid for nybid, the AtomicPolygon topology for nyhez and nycdwi); everything else reads the valid polygon either way. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the features it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-20): 10 on 26c. With it on, the geometry and part counts differ from prod's and SHAPE_Area still matches.
decision: match prod by default (published as stored); valid polygons behind make_valid_district_polygons (off)

scope: nycb2010(wi) on 12-14 blocks and nycb2020(wi) on 6-7; nyct2010wi/nyct2020wi tract 1000100; nycc/nyccwi districts 38 and 47; nymc/nymcwi 301, 305 and 404
description: Prod's census block and tract, council district and municipal court layers disagree with the current AtomicPolygons in a few places, and with prod's own ThinLION, ThinED and LION. Most weren't regenerated after recent AtomicPolygon edits. Three blocks are the same kind of disagreement: 10223003005 is keyed to tract 022300, which doesn't exist (the AtomicPolygon and prod's LION say 10223013005); water block 10001001000, and so water tract 1000100, reaches 1,417 sq ft past every AtomicPolygon; and 39901000008 includes AtomicPolygon 3990100031, whose block is 0007.
decision: keep ours

scope: nypp precincts 17, 19, 23, 50, 61, 63, 72 and 88
description: Ours clips the NYPD source precincts to land and drops the parts and holes under 100 sq ft the clip leaves. Prod keeps some of them: tiny parts 28 to 2,700 ft from the rest of the precinct, so the outlines differ by far more than their area.
decision: keep ours

scope: nypp precinct 113
description: Prod clipped precinct 113 to a different Jamaica Bay / JFK shoreline than its own nybb uses: the 43,419 sq ft only ours has all lies inside prod's nybb (Queens), and only 7 of the 31,844 sq ft only prod has does. The pieces follow AtomicPolygon water_flag 2 (ours) against 1 (prod) along the shore. Ours clips to the same land as every other layer; the outlines differ by about 0.02% of the area.
decision: keep ours

scope: nynta2010 CountyFIPS where the NTA's NeighborhoodPUMACodes row has a blank FIPS code (none on 26c)
description: Prod looks CountyFIPS up in the NTA's NeighborhoodPUMACodes row and leaves it blank where the FIPS code is blank, logging the blank code (GDBExtractorClass.cs:1597-1621). We reproduce prod by default; the dbt var fill_nta_county_fips_from_borough (default false) fills it from the NTA's borough instead, which maps to exactly one county. With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the NTAs it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-16): none on 26c.
decision: match prod by default (CountyFIPS blank); borough fill behind fill_nta_county_fips_from_borough (off)

scope: nyct2010 and nyct2010wi water tract 990100 (Lower Bay) in Brooklyn and Staten Island: BoroCT2010 and NTACode
description: The source census tract layer's BOROCT reads 4990100 (a Queens tract) and its NEIGHBORHOOD_CODE QN99 on the Brooklyn and Staten Island pieces of tract 990100 as well as the Queens one. Prod copies them (DistrictBoundaryGDBExtractorConfiguration.xml: BoroCT2010 <- BoroCT, NTACode <- Neighborhood_Code, NTAName looked up by that code; GDBExtractorClass.cs:960-1000, 1597-1621), so its nyct2010wi carries 4990100 on all three pieces and its nyct2010 on the Staten Island land piece. We reproduce prod by default. The dbt var key_tracts_by_borough (default false) keys each piece by its borough and tract instead (3990100, 4990100, 5990100), as the AtomicPolygons, the census block layers, LION and ThinLION do, with its NTA by borough and tract (BK99, QN99, SI99). With it off there is no difference; every build's log reports the tracts it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-21): 2 on 26c. The geometry is the same either way.
decision: match prod by default (source BOROCT and NEIGHBORHOOD_CODE); borough keys behind key_tracts_by_borough (off)

scope: Generic and physical records whose ID is deleted on another segment, 12 records on 26c
description: Prod drops any record, other than a delete, whose new or journalled old ID is deleted anywhere in this release's edit journal: on any segment, at any time, among deletes of its own record type and of the types written before it (S, then G, then P; IsSegmentdeleted in CSCLEditor.dll's LDFExtractHelper). One generic or physical ID spans many segments, so for G and P this drops reassignments LION shows took effect, e.g. segment 0003939's generic 192146 to 192147 and segment 0215581's 102207 to 192223. We reproduce prod by default; the fix (dbt var fix_ldf_journal_delete_scope, default false) drops a G or P record only when its ID is deleted on the same node pair, among deletes of its own type, and is off until GR agrees to roll it out. With it off there is no difference: LDF.dat's records and LDF.header match prod. Every build's log reports the records it would change (CSCL-LOG-OURS-11): on 26c, 6 G/P reassignments, 2 splits and 4 merges (6 G and 6 P records), which with the fix on also raise the header's record count by 12 and renumber later records (CSCL-LDF-03). Which is right is a question for GR.
decision: match prod by default; fix available behind fix_ldf_journal_delete_scope (off)

scope: Cumulative record number (positions 91-100)
description: On 26c both headers carry 0000570027 and both sides number from 570028. By default (fix_ldf_journal_delete_scope off, CSCL-LDF-01) both files hold the same 2,400 records, and 162 lines differ (77 G, 85 P), in record order only: both sort a block by action code, new ID and old ID, and records that tie on those (one ID's reassignment along several segments) keep journal order. Prod's writer sorts a DataTable it filled from the journal sorted by CHANGE_DATETIME, and the sort keeps that order among ties (LDFExtractHelper.cs, CreateTransitoryDataTable and WriteToLDFExtractFile); ours takes CHANGE_DATETIME, then LDF_NUM, under both flag settings, since it is ordering and not the delete rule. CHANGE_DATETIME is to the second, and all 162 are records journalled in the same second, whose order in prod the source doesn't record: no journal column (LDF_NUM, OBJECTID, VERSION_NUM, GLOBALID, node IDs) reproduces it better. Only with the fix on, its 12 extra records shift every later number too: 1,410 lines differ then. Separately, prod's base number is typed in by hand (its sequence has a gap, 25B to 25C) while ours continues from the previous edition's header, so the base can drift too. QA compares positions 1-90 only.

scope: ABCEGNPX G/N/X side AtomicPolygon, 1 row per file each for placeids 1031192 and 1041121
description: Prod places a CommonPlace point within the source's XY tolerance (0.0002 ft) of an AtomicPolygon boundary in the lowest-OBJECTID AtomicPolygon within that tolerance (Esri treats the point as on the boundary). Ours applies the same rule (SAFExtractClass.cs:1851-1865: Within, then Intersects, first feature; ArcObjectsHelpersClass.cs:1056, 1120) and matches prod on the other 119 of the 121 26c points in that tolerance; on these two prod took the higher-OBJECTID AtomicPolygon. Both lie on a curved AtomicPolygon boundary, which we load linearized (within 0.00025 ft of the true arc), and the linearization puts each on the other side: on the true arcs each lies inside the AtomicPolygon prod took, 0.000075 and 0.000146 ft from its boundary, so still within the tolerance of both. Neither rule reproduces prod there: the one other 26c point near a curved boundary in that tolerance (placeid 1035819) is 0.000005 ft inside the higher-OBJECTID AtomicPolygon on the true arcs, and prod took the lowest-OBJECTID one.
decision: keep ours
